source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During a chest x-ray, what is the client asked to do?
questions.rationale: The client stands in front of the film, inhales deeply, and holds the breath while images are taken.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chest X-ray (PDF p. 60)
questions.quote: Ask the client to inhale deeply and hold his or her breath while the x-ray images are taken

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which SpO2 reading is considered normal?
questions.rationale: Normal pulse oximetry is 95% or more; lower values suggest hypoxemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Oximetry (PDF p. 61)
questions.quote: Greater than or equal to 95%

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What should be done before applying a finger pulse oximeter?
questions.rationale: Remove false nails and polish; warming the finger improves blood flow.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Oximetry (PDF p. 61)
questions.quote: Ensure that the patient does not have false fingernails and that nail polish has been removed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How much pleural fluid may be removed in the first 30 minutes of thoracentesis?
questions.rationale: No more than 1000 mL is removed within the first 30 minutes to avoid complications such as re-expansion edema.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thoracentesis (PDF p. 62)
questions.quote: Don't remove more than 1.000 ml of fluid from the pleural cavity within the first 30 minutes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After thoracentesis, how is the client positioned for 1 hour?
questions.rationale: Post-thoracentesis, the client sits or lies on the unaffected side for 1 hour.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thoracentesis (PDF p. 62)
questions.quote: Position: sitting or side-lying (unaffected side) for 1 hour

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In Allen's test, color should return within how many seconds?
questions.rationale: If color returns within 6 seconds after releasing the ulnar artery, collateral circulation is adequate.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Allen's Test (PDF p. 62)
questions.quote: If blood is restored within 6 seconds

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The total air exhaled after a maximal inspiration is the:
questions.rationale: Vital capacity is the maximum air exhaled after maximal inspiration.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulmonary Function (PDF p. 63)
questions.quote: Vital Capacity Total amount of air that can be exhaled after a maximal inspiration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which medication should be held for 4 hours before pulmonary function tests?
questions.rationale: Avoid bronchodilators for at least 4 hours and smoking or heavy meals for 4–6 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulmonary Function (PDF p. 63)
questions.quote: Client should avoid bronchodilators for at least 4 hours before the study

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During pulmonary angiography dye injection, what may the client feel?
questions.rationale: Clients may feel burning and flushing, an urge to cough, nausea, or a salty metallic taste.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulmonary Angiography (PDF p. 64)
questions.quote: a burning and flushing sensation may be felt throughout the body during injection

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why does the nurse mark peripheral pulses before angiography?
questions.rationale: Marking pulses allows comparison of circulation after the procedure; bed rest is kept 4–6 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulmonary Angiography (PDF p. 64)
questions.quote: Mark the site of the client’s peripheral pulses before angiography using pen

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a barium swallow, what stool change should the client expect for 2–3 days?
questions.rationale: Stools are white or light for 2–3 days; report if they do not return to normal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Barium Swallow (PDF p. 65)
questions.quote: stools will be white or light in color for 2 to 3 days

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What diet is given 2 days before a barium enema?
questions.rationale: Low-residue and clear-liquid diets 2 days before, NPO 8 hours, plus laxatives.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Barium Enema (PDF p. 65)
questions.quote: Low-residue and clear-liquid diet 2 days before the procedure

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How is the client positioned for colonoscopy?
questions.rationale: Colonoscopy uses the Sims' (left lateral, knees flexed) position.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colonoscopy (PDF p. 66)
questions.quote: Position: Sim’s position / Left side with knees flexed

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why does the nurse ask about oral iron the week before colonoscopy?
questions.rationale: Oral iron within a week causes black, sticky stool that impairs visualization.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colonoscopy (PDF p. 66)
questions.quote: Note intake of oral iron preparations within 1 week before the procedure

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After colonoscopy, which sign suggests perforation?
questions.rationale: Belching and flatus are from air insufflation; pain, distention, bleeding, or fever suggest perforation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colonoscopy (PDF p. 66)
questions.quote: Observe for signs and symptoms of bowel perforation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How many stool specimens are taken for a guaiac (occult blood) test?
questions.rationale: Three specimens on consecutive days are taken.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fecalysis (PDF p. 67)
questions.quote: Taken in 3 consecutive days (3 stool specimens)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should a stool specimen for ova and parasites be handled?
questions.rationale: O&P specimens are sent immediately, fresh and warm, often to detect amoebiasis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stool Exam (PDF p. 67)
questions.quote: Specimen should be sent immediately (fresh and warm)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which instruction applies to a 72-hour stool fat collection?
questions.rationale: Fats are included in the diet; alcohol and mineral oil are avoided.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stool for Lipids (PDF p. 67)
questions.quote: Avoid mineral oil and other oily medications.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How is the client positioned for proctosigmoidoscopy?
questions.rationale: Left lateral decubitus or knee-chest position is used.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Proctosigmoidoscopy (PDF p. 66)
questions.quote: Position: left lateral decubitus position/ knee-chest position

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which older adult finding after bronchoscopy needs attention?
questions.rationale: Older clients are assessed for confusion and lethargy after sedation; NPO until gag returns.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bronchoscopy (PDF p. 61)
questions.quote: For elderly patients, nurse assesses for confusion and lethargy
